program.help:
Detect and decompose spike collision waveforms into their single-unit components.
Must be run AFTER spike sorting (ndm_klustakwik) and manual curation in Klusters. Requires .clu.N, .res.N, and .spk.N files for each spike group.
When two neurons fire within roughly one spike-width of each other (~1 ms), their extracellular waveforms sum linearly and the recorded composite waveform lands between the two parent clusters in feature space. These "collision spikes" inflate false-positive and false-negative rates and corrupt cross-correlograms near zero lag. This plugin identifies and decomposes them post-curation, without modifying the original spike-sorting files.
All template matching is performed within a single spikeDetection group (same shank). Cross-shank collisions are not attempted because their spatial overlap at individual electrode sites is negligible.
ALGORITHM
1. Template building A mean waveform template is computed for each curated unit that fired at least minSpikesTemplate spikes. The per-unit peak-to-peak amplitude distribution on the dominant channel is stored for the acceptance gate.
2. Single-template screening Each spike is correlated against all templates at shifts in [-maxShiftSamp, +maxShiftSamp] samples. Spikes whose best-match Pearson r exceeds corrThreshold are well explained by a single unit and skipped. Spikes below the minSnrRms noise gate are also skipped.
3. Two-component matching pursuit For each candidate, two greedy passes find (unit, shift, amplitude) pairs that minimise the residual waveform energy. A decomposition is accepted when: - The residual energy is < residualThreshold * original energy (default 25%) - Both component amplitudes fall within the 1st-99th percentile of their unit's empirical amplitude distribution (rejects unphysical solutions) - Both amplitudes are positive (no anti-phase solutions) Sub-sample shift precision is achieved via parabolic interpolation around the integer-sample optimum, identical to the drift estimator's xcorr peak.
4. Output One SESSION.col.N sidecar file per spikeDetection group (YAML format). The original .clu.N, .res.N and .spk.N files are NOT modified.
OUTPUT FILE SESSION.col.N collisions: format: '1.0' spikeGroup: 1 nSpikes: 14302 nTemplates: 6 nCandidates: 847 nDecomposed: 312 spikes: - spikeIndex: 47 timestamp: 19423 collision_accepted: true component1: { unitId: 3, shiftSamp: -4, shiftFrac: -3.82, amplitude: 1.03 } component2: { unitId: 2, shiftSamp: 6, shiftFrac: 6.14, amplitude: 0.97 } residualNorm: 0.19
DOWNSTREAM USE collision_accepted == true → exclude spike from single-unit analyses, OR re-assign as two events at timestamp+shiftSamp_1 (unit k1) and timestamp+shiftSamp_2 (unit k2). collision_accepted == false → spike is a candidate but decomposition was not convincing; treat as unresolved.
OPTIONAL PARAMETERS
# maxShiftSamp Maximum temporal shift (±samples) when scanning template matches. At 32 kHz, 10 samples ≈ 0.31 ms. Increase to ~16 for slower acquisition rates or probes with wider waveforms. Larger values increase runtime quadratically. (default = 10)
# corrThreshold Pearson r threshold below which a spike is flagged as a collision candidate. Increase toward 0.92 to flag only the most obvious collisions; decrease toward 0.75 to cast a wider net (more candidates, more false positives in stage 3). (default = 0.85)
# residualThreshold Maximum fractional residual energy ||R|| / ||W|| for an accepted decomposition. 0.25 means the two-template model must explain ≥75% of the waveform energy. Tighten to 0.15 for high-SNR recordings; relax to 0.35 for noisy data. (default = 0.25)
# minSnrRms Minimum spike amplitude in units of estimated RMS noise (Quiroga 2004 MAD estimator). Spikes below this level cannot be reliably decomposed and are skipped regardless of their template correlation. (default = 4.0)
# minSpikesTemplate Minimum number of spikes a curated unit must have contributed to be used as a template. Units with fewer spikes have noisy mean waveforms that degrade decomposition accuracy. (default = 30)
# excludeNoise If true (default), cluster 0 (artifact) and cluster 1 (MUA) are excluded from template building. Their waveforms are too heterogeneous to serve as reliable collision components. Set to false only if MUA was intentionally curated. (default = true)
# overwrite If false (default), skip groups whose .col.N file already exists. Set to true to force recomputation after changing parameters. (default = false)
